extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, apprentices, and other apprenticeship stakeholders (and public commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and compliance criteria for U.S. registered apprenticeship programs under the Department of Labor's proposed part 29 rulemaking, covering National Guidelines/Occupational Standards alignment, end-point assessments, complaints, recordkeeping, and program reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards may be used by sponsors seeking registration, including in occupations where National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship (NOSA) have not been developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines are an existing tool for national organizations and can be adjusted based on local workforce needs or conditions (per OA Circular No. 2022-02). The requirement to use existing NOSA applies only when the Administrator has already approved NOSA for an occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: When National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship have been developed and approved for an occupation, National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards submitted for that occupation must substantially align with the approved NOSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor modifications to NOSA may be allowed based on sponsor needs, but submissions must substantially align with industry-validated standards. The Department seeks comment on what deviations are acceptable without undermining the occupation or quality of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable Deviations from National Occupational Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviations from approved NOSA are permitted so long as the National Guidelines substantially align with NOSA and do not undermine occupation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable modifications include additions of sponsor- or employer-specific training beyond the approved framework, addition of competencies or on-the-job training hours to achieve competencies, and addition of academic-credit-bearing related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-Point Assessment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered apprenticeship programs must administer an end-point assessment at the conclusion of the apprenticeship term to establish successful attainment of all knowledge, skills, and competencies associated with the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment is intended as objective confirmation of proficiency; the end-point assessment should be the culminating activity and a Certificate of Completion should be awarded only upon successful completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-Point Assessment Purpose and Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: End-point assessments provide objective confirmation that an apprentice has acquired occupation-relevant competency, improving employer confidence, apprentice employability, and labor mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A uniform, rigorous standard benefits employers and apprentices and aligns with international best practices (e.g., Canada's Red Seal). The Department views these benefits as outweighing additional sponsor burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-Point Assessment Content and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: End-point assessments may include practical hands-on components, written components assessing theoretical knowledge, a combination, or other methods such as individual performance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may develop assessments according to program parameters. The Department does not propose a specific assessment type but invites comments on whether assessments should be required to objectively measure attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Occupational Proficiency (safety, accuracy, timeliness, efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments should measure not only task competency (safety and accuracy) but also overall occupational proficiency including timeliness and efficiency where relevant to business needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proficiency includes being able to perform tasks safely and accurately as well as within timeframes that make work profitable or meet customer demands; sponsors should consider these outcomes when designing assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration: Sponsor vs Independent/Third-Party Assessors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes value in both sponsor-developed assessments and independent/third-party assessments to reduce bias and incorporate outside perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department invites comment on whether assessments should be performed by independent organizations or by program operators, and on whether final rules should require objective, qualified examiners who have not previously provided OJT or related instruction to the apprentice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Third-Party or State-Mandated Examinations as End-Point Assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors may be permitted to utilize third-party examinations as the program's end-point assessment in certain instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two examples: (1) an independent certification body offers a nationally recognized exam incorporating industry-recognized standards; or (2) the occupation requires a State-mandated/licensure exam. The Department invites comments on permitting these uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retake Opportunities for End-Point Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: An apprentice must be entitled to at least one additional opportunity to complete an end-point assessment if they do not pass on the first attempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures fairness and reduces the assessment operating as an inequitable barrier (e.g., for apprentices with disabilities). The Department requests input on whether to limit the number of opportunities balancing burden and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Accommodations for Assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: An apprentice's end-point assessment must include appropriate reasonable accommodations if requested prior to administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to ensure registered apprenticeship programs are accessible to job seekers with disabilities and aligns with ACA DEIA recommendations to identify and remove access barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Completion Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who successfully complete on-the-job training and related instruction requirements and pass an end-point assessment are eligible for a Certificate of Completion from the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate issuance is tied to passing the end-point assessment; the Department contemplates greater standardization via National Occupational Standards but currently does not prescribe a single assessment type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints: Who May File and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprentices and non-apprentices may file complaints so long as the complaint arises under a registered apprenticeship agreement or alleges a violation of part 29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule carries forward existing provisions but expands who can file; Registration Agencies remain prohibited from resolving complaints covered by collective bargaining agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Resolution Before Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Disputes may be resolved locally before filing a complaint with the Registration Agency, but this is permitted, not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes program sponsors often resolve issues efficiently; however, a direct filing route is available especially for egregious matters or when complainants wish to remain anonymous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Filing Deadline (300 days) and Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be filed within 300 calendar days after the conclusion of the events giving rise to the dispute or alleged violation; for continuing violations, the 300 days begins when the violation ceases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies may extend the filing time for good cause (e.g., late awareness, illness, injury). The 300-day period aligns with 29 CFR part 30 and balances timeliness and quality-control needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints must include a means of contacting the complainant or authorized representative, the identity of the individual or entity alleged responsible, and a short description of the events (including when they occurred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring contact means facilitates anonymous complaints while enabling the Agency to follow up; the prior signature requirement is removed to facilitate anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency Investigation Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must proceed expeditiously to investigate complaints, provide written notice of receipt, investigate complete complaints, and complete a thorough investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should be completed before impacted apprentices finish programs where possible. The Department seeks comment on whether to set a uniform ceiling for investigation completion time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Investigation Documentation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint files should include the complaint, any respondent rebuttal, interview statements, copies of pertinent documents, and a narrative report of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A robust file is necessary to demonstrate that adequate investigation occurred, to facilitate further review, referrals, or program review initiation. Agencies should protect witness identifying information consistent with privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Investigation Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency must provide written notification of its findings to the complainant and respondent at the conclusion of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial notice of receipt is provided to complainant and authorized representative; final findings are shared with complainant and respondent to close the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Complainant Identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency must protect the identity of the complainant to the extent practicable; anonymous complaints must be filed directly with the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps include not naming the complainant in interviews or in responses to sponsor inquiries. Investigators should confer with complainants early to discuss investigation steps that preserve anonymity, recognizing identities may still be deduced in small programs or workplace-specific disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation Outcomes and Remedial Options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Agency determines a violation of part 29 or the apprenticeship agreement occurred, it should attempt to resolve the violation quickly through technical assistance, program review initiation, or deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides graduated responses depending on severity and aims to correct issues promptly to protect apprentices and program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-Retaliation Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a broad range of adverse actions (intimidation, threats, coercion, retaliation, discrimination) and protects activities including filing a complaint, opposing prohibited practices, furnishing information, or exercising rights under part 29 or an apprenticeship agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-retaliation complaints cannot be filed anonymously because Agencies must reveal the complainant's identity to seek a remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and Remedies for Retaliation by Sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors who fail to prevent or remedy retaliation may face remedies including making the apprentice whole (reinstatement to same step with back pay plus interest), limiting responsibilities of persons responsible for misconduct, or deregistration under §29.20(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumptive remedy for termination for filing a complaint is reinstatement with back pay and interest; Agencies may pursue other tailored remedies depending on misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Recordkeeping Obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors and participating employers must maintain records the Registration Agency considers necessary to determine compliance with part 29 and applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping is essential for program reviews and complaint investigations. The Department seeks comment on adding or subtracting records from the proposed list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Employment Decision Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must maintain records concerning employment decisions: hiring/placement, promotion, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, right of return from layoff, and rehiring of apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are typically maintained in the ordinary course of business and are paramount because registered apprenticeship rests on employment of apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Program Operation Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records related to the operation of the registered apprenticeship program, including program standards, apprenticeship agreements, completion records, cancellation and suspension records, and program review files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records complement employment decision records and are necessary to demonstrate compliance with proposed §§29.8–29.10 and program review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Apprentice Performance and Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of each apprentice's performance and progress in both on-the-job training and related instruction components, including records related to end-point assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are needed to demonstrate progress and attainment of competency, and relate to work process schedules and wage progression; competency attainment measures are critical for sponsor retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Interim Credentials and Academic Credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records pertaining to an apprentice's attainment of interim credentials, postsecondary academic credit, or other interim milestones during program participation, if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule asks sponsors to disclose interim credentials; where provided, documentation must be kept to validate credential attainment as a program quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Hours, Wages, and Fringe Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records for each apprentice regarding number of hours of on-the-job training, number of hours of related instruction, total hours worked, and wages and fringe benefits paid for all hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records are integral to standards of apprenticeship and apprenticeship agreements and essential to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Non-EEO Complaint-Related Personnel Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain personnel records applicable to any non-EEO complaints filed with the Registration Agency under proposed §29.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records support investigation and adjudication of complaints outside EEO channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Safety and Health Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records related to sponsor and participating employers' safety records, including safety and health training provided to apprentices, incident logs required under Federal/State laws, and current workers' compensation documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such records are required where applicable to demonstrate compliance with occupational safety and health obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Records Required by Part 30 and Title 38
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain any records required by 29 CFR part 30 and any records required under title 38, U.S. Code (for veterans' educational assistance eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consistency across related regulatory requirements and enables use of veterans' educational assistance for program enrollment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Documents Demonstrating Compliance with Federal Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records demonstrating program compliance with registered apprenticeship requirements to meet Federal purposes (e.g., documents for compliance with Federal grants like WIOA, IRA, Davis-Bacon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents help validate that programs satisfy Federal grant or statutory obligations tied to apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention Period
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by this part must be maintained for 5 years from the date of making of the record or the personnel action involved, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 5-year timeframe aligns with 29 CFR 30.12 and the proposed 5-year program review cadence. Failure to preserve complete and accurate records constitutes noncompliance and may lead to deregistration proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency Access to Records and Format Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors (and participating employers) must allow Registration Agencies access to records upon request for program reviews and complaint investigations, including inspecting and copying books, accounts, and electronic records, and must provide information about formats in which records are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information obtained will be used only in connection with administration of part 29 or other applicable laws. Sponsors should provide specific electronic format information when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Medium Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms, records, and documents may exist in paper, electronic, or combined form, but regardless of medium they must be available and accessible as required for oversight and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acknowledges mixed media recordkeeping practices but requires sponsors to ensure access for Registration Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Reviews: Purpose and Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Program reviews are the linchpin for quality standards, worker protections, transparency, and accountability; they should be clear, transparent, and fair and provide opportunity for program improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed section encapsulates the review process and aligns with current practice of allowing programs time to address issues internally and request guidance; reviews are both enforcement tools and opportunities to identify near- and long-term program quality improvements.
